newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian minister defends civil servant pensions.
newsitem.headline: Belgian minister defends civil servant pensions.

text.p: Belgian Interior Affairs Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Johan Vande Lanotte said on Monday current civil servant pensions should remain untouched in the upcoming reform of the system.

"The same thing goes for the reform of civil servant pensions as for the reform of private sector pensions: we are not touching existing pensions," Vande Lanotte told Belgian daily Het Laatste Nieuws.
Vande Lanotte is one of the top socialist ministers in Belgium's centre-left coalition government.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, a christian-democrat, indicated that he wanted to reduce current civil servant pensions.
"We must wonder whether every margin for wage increases for civil servants should be limited by the obligation for similar increases for civil servant pensions," he Belgian television.
Belgian civil servant pensions rise in line with civil servant salaries.
In the 1997 budget, approved by parliament last week, it was decided to raise the retirement age for women to 65 years from 60 within 13 years.
The budget introduced some austerity measures for private sector pensions but left the civil servant pensions untouched.
Last Friday, Belgium's socialist civil servant unions called for a national strike in all public services if the government embarks on a reform of their pension system.
One of Dehaene's top priorities is the long-awaited reform of Belgium's generous social security system. The reform is expected to be the focus of government policy in coming months.
